Content:
The following two identities are known as the sum and difference formulas for tangent:
[MATH: \tan (x + y)|= (\tan x + \tan y)/(1 − \tan x\tan y); \tan (x − y)|= (\tan x − \tan y)/(1 + \tan x\tan y)]

Content:
We can use the sum and difference rules to find the exact values of some trigonometric ratios. For example, let's use the sum rule to find the value of

Content:
[MATH: \tan(75^\circ).]

Content:
We start by writing [MATH: 75^\circ] as a sum of special angles:

Content:
[MATH: 75^\circ = {\color{blue}45^\circ} + {\color{red}30^\circ}]

Content:
We now apply the sum formula for tangent as follows:

Content:
[MATH: \tan (75^{∘})|= \tan (30^{∘} + 45^{∘}); = (\tan 30^{∘} + \tan 45^{∘})/(1 − \tan 30^{∘}\tan 45^{∘}); = (((sqrt(3))/(3) + 1))/((1 − (sqrt(3))/(3) ⋅ 1)); = (((sqrt(3))/(3) + 1))/((1 − (sqrt(3))/(3)))]

Content:
We can simplify this fraction by multiplying the numerator and denominator by [MATH: 3\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: \tan (75^{∘})|= (((sqrt(3))/(3) + 1))/((1 − (sqrt(3))/(3))); = (3 ⋅ ((sqrt(3))/(3) + 1))/(3 ⋅ (1 − (sqrt(3))/(3))); = (sqrt(3) + 3)/(3 − sqrt(3)); = (3 + sqrt(3))/(3 − sqrt(3))]

Content:
Finally, we rationalize the denominator:

Content:
[MATH: \tan (75^{∘})|= (3 + sqrt(3))/(3 − sqrt(3)); = (3 + sqrt(3))/(3 − sqrt(3)) ⋅ (3 + sqrt(3))/(3 + sqrt(3)); = (3^{2} + 6sqrt(3) + (sqrt(3))^{2})/(3^{2} − (sqrt(3))^{2}); = (9 + 6sqrt(3) + 3)/(9 − 3); = (12 + 6sqrt(3))/(6); = 2 + sqrt(3)]

Content:
Therefore, we conclude that

Content:
[MATH: \tan (75^\circ) = 2+\sqrt 3.]

sections.readable_text:
Find the exact value of [MATH: \tan \left( \dfrac{\pi}{12} \right).]

Hint: Use the fact that [MATH: \dfrac{\pi}{12} = \dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{4}.]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Recall the difference formula for tangent: [MATH: \tan(x-y) = \dfrac{\tan{x}-\tan{y}}{1+\tan{x}\tan{y}}]

Applying the difference formula for tangent with [MATH: x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}] and [MATH: y = \dfrac{\pi}{4},] we obtain

[MATH: \tan ((π)/(12))|= \tan ((π)/(3) − (π)/(4)); = (\tan ((π)/(3)) − \tan ((π)/(4)))/(1 + \tan ((π)/(3))\tan ((π)/(4))); = (sqrt(3) − 1)/(1 + sqrt(3) ⋅ 1); = (sqrt(3) − 1)/(sqrt(3) + 1).]

Finally, we rationalize the denominator:

[MATH: \tan ((π)/(12))|= (sqrt(3) − 1)/(sqrt(3) + 1); = (sqrt(3) − 1)/(sqrt(3) + 1) ⋅ (sqrt(3) − 1)/(sqrt(3) − 1); = ((sqrt(3))^{2} − 2sqrt(3) + (− 1)^{2})/((sqrt(3))^{2} − 1^{2}); = (3 − 2sqrt(3) + 1)/(3 − 1); = (4 − 2sqrt(3))/(2); = 2 − sqrt(3)]

sections.normalized_html: If [MATH: \tan x = -\dfrac {4\sqrt 3} 3], then find the value of [MATH: \tan (x -30^\circ).]
sections.readable_text: If [MATH: \tan x = -\dfrac {4\sqrt 3} 3], then find the value of [MATH: \tan (x -30^\circ).]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
First, we recall the difference formula for tangent:

[MATH: \tan(u-v) = \dfrac{\tan{u}-\tan{v}}{1+\tan{u}\tan{v}}]

Applying the sum formula for tangent with [MATH: u=x] and [MATH: v=30^{\circ},] we obtain

[MATH: \eqalign{ \tan(x -30^\circ) &= \dfrac{\tan x - \tan 30^\circ}{1 + \tan x \tan 30^\circ} \[5pt] &= \dfrac{\left(-\dfrac{4 \sqrt 3}3 -\dfrac{1} {\sqrt 3}\right)}{\left(1+\left(-\dfrac{4 \sqrt 3}3\right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\right)} \[5pt] &= \dfrac{\left(-\dfrac {4\sqrt 3} 3 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt 3}\cdot \dfrac{\sqrt 3} { \sqrt 3}\right)} {\left(1-\dfrac 43\right)} \[5pt] &= \dfrac{\left(-\dfrac {4\sqrt 3} 3 - \dfrac{\sqrt 3} { 3}\right)} {\left(-\dfrac 13\right)} \[5pt] & = \dfrac {\left(- \dfrac{5\sqrt 3}{3}\right)} {\left( -\dfrac 1 3 \right)}\[3pt] & = 5\sqrt{3}. }]

items.readable_text:
Content:
We've practiced using the sum and difference formulas for tangent. But where do they come from?

Content:
To derive the sum formula for tangent, we start off by recalling the sum and difference formulas for sine and cosine:

Content:
[MATH: \sin (x + y)|= \sin x\cos y + \cos x\sin y; \cos (x + y)|= \cos x\cos y − \sin x\sin y]

Content:
Now, using the identity [MATH: \tan\theta = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta},] we can divide [MATH: \sin(x+ y)] by [MATH: \cos(x+ y)] to get [MATH: \tan(x+ y).] Dividing, we have

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{\sin(x+ y)}{\cos(x+ y)} = \dfrac{\sin x\cos y + \cos x\sin y}{\cos x\cos y - \sin x\sin y},]

Content:
and simplifying, we reach

Content:
[MATH: \tan(x+y) = \dfrac{\sin x\cos y + \cos x\sin y}{\cos x\cos y - \sin x\sin y}.]

Content:
To write the right-hand side in terms of tangent only, we divide the numerator and denominator by [MATH: \cos x\cos y.] This gives

Content:
[MATH: \tan (x + y)|= (\sin x\cos y + \cos x\sin y)/(\cos x\cos y − \sin x\sin y); = (((\sin x\cos y)/(\cos x\cos y) + (\cos x\sin y)/(\cos x\cos y)))/(((\cos x\cos y)/(\cos x\cos y) − (\sin x\sin y)/(\cos x\cos y))); = (((\sin x\cos y)/(\cos x\cos y) + (\cos x\sin y)/(\cos x\cos y)))/((1 − (\sin x\sin y)/(\cos x\cos y))); = (((\sin x)/(\cos x) + (\sin y)/(\cos y)))/((1 − (\sin x)/(\cos x) ⋅ (\sin y)/(\cos y))); = (\tan x + \tan y)/(1 − \tan x\tan y).]

Content:
We can derive the difference formula for tangent in a similar way.

Example Prompt:
Find the exact value of [MATH: \tan \left( \dfrac{\pi}{12} \right).]

Hint: Use the fact that [MATH: \dfrac{\pi}{12} = \dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\pi}{4}.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Recall the difference formula for tangent:
[MATH: \tan(x-y) = \dfrac{\tan{x}-\tan{y}}{1+\tan{x}\tan{y}}]

Applying the difference formula for tangent with [MATH: x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}] and [MATH: y = \dfrac{\pi}{4},] we obtain

[MATH: \tan ((π)/(12))|= \tan ((π)/(3) − (π)/(4)); = (\tan ((π)/(3)) − \tan ((π)/(4)))/(1 + \tan ((π)/(3))\tan ((π)/(4))); = (sqrt(3) − 1)/(1 + sqrt(3) ⋅ 1); = (sqrt(3) − 1)/(sqrt(3) + 1).]

Finally, we rationalize the denominator:

[MATH: \tan ((π)/(12))|= (sqrt(3) − 1)/(sqrt(3) + 1); = (sqrt(3) − 1)/(sqrt(3) + 1) ⋅ (sqrt(3) − 1)/(sqrt(3) − 1); = ((sqrt(3))^{2} − 2sqrt(3) + (− 1)^{2})/((sqrt(3))^{2} − 1^{2}); = (3 − 2sqrt(3) + 1)/(3 − 1); = (4 − 2sqrt(3))/(2); = 2 − sqrt(3)]

Item 5 — Example: Simplifying an Expression Using the Sum and Difference Formulas: Degrees

Example Prompt:
If [MATH: \tan x = -\dfrac {4\sqrt 3} 3], then find the value of [MATH: \tan (x -30^\circ).]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
First, we recall the difference formula for tangent:

[MATH: \tan(u-v) = \dfrac{\tan{u}-\tan{v}}{1+\tan{u}\tan{v}}]

Applying the sum formula for tangent with [MATH: u=x] and [MATH: v=30^{\circ},] we obtain

[MATH: \eqalign{
\tan(x -30^\circ)
&= \dfrac{\tan x - \tan 30^\circ}{1 + \tan x \tan 30^\circ} \[5pt]
&= \dfrac{\left(-\dfrac{4 \sqrt 3}3 -\dfrac{1} {\sqrt 3}\right)}{\left(1+\left(-\dfrac{4 \sqrt 3}3\right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\right)} \[5pt]
&= \dfrac{\left(-\dfrac {4\sqrt 3} 3 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt 3}\cdot \dfrac{\sqrt 3} { \sqrt 3}\right)} {\left(1-\dfrac 43\right)} \[5pt]
&= \dfrac{\left(-\dfrac {4\sqrt 3} 3 - \dfrac{\sqrt 3} { 3}\right)} {\left(-\dfrac 13\right)} \[5pt]
& = \dfrac {\left(- \dfrac{5\sqrt 3}{3}\right)} {\left( -\dfrac 1 3 \right)}\[3pt]
& = 5\sqrt{3}.

}]

Item 11 — Tutorial: Deriving the Sum and Difference Formulas for Tangent

Content:
We've practiced using the sum and difference formulas for tangent. But where do they come from?

Content:
To derive the sum formula for tangent, we start off by recalling the sum and difference formulas for sine and cosine:

Content:
[MATH: \sin (x + y)|= \sin x\cos y + \cos x\sin y; \cos (x + y)|= \cos x\cos y − \sin x\sin y]

Content:
Now, using the identity [MATH: \tan\theta = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta},] we can divide [MATH: \sin(x+ y)] by [MATH: \cos(x+ y)] to get [MATH: \tan(x+ y).] Dividing, we have

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{\sin(x+ y)}{\cos(x+ y)} = \dfrac{\sin x\cos y + \cos x\sin y}{\cos x\cos y - \sin x\sin y},]

Content:
and simplifying, we reach

Content:
[MATH: \tan(x+y) = \dfrac{\sin x\cos y + \cos x\sin y}{\cos x\cos y - \sin x\sin y}.]

Content:
To write the right-hand side in terms of tangent only, we divide the numerator and denominator by [MATH: \cos x\cos y.] This gives

Content:
[MATH: \tan (x + y)|= (\sin x\cos y + \cos x\sin y)/(\cos x\cos y − \sin x\sin y); = (((\sin x\cos y)/(\cos x\cos y) + (\cos x\sin y)/(\cos x\cos y)))/(((\cos x\cos y)/(\cos x\cos y) − (\sin x\sin y)/(\cos x\cos y))); = (((\sin x\cos y)/(\cos x\cos y) + (\cos x\sin y)/(\cos x\cos y)))/((1 − (\sin x\sin y)/(\cos x\cos y))); = (((\sin x)/(\cos x) + (\sin y)/(\cos y)))/((1 − (\sin x)/(\cos x) ⋅ (\sin y)/(\cos y))); = (\tan x + \tan y)/(1 − \tan x\tan y).]

Content:
We can derive the difference formula for tangent in a similar way.
